extName.description: The extension's name in Firefox (brand: keep)

extDescription.message: Checks that each Flagship server you visit serves the certificate it signed, and spots Flagship sign-in pages. Pairs with the Flagship app; holds no key that can act as you.

badgeMatch.message: Flagship: this site's certificate is the one your server signed

badgeMismatch.message: Flagship stopped this site: its certificate isn't the one your server signed

badgeStale.message: Flagship: this site's certificate matches, but your server hasn't confirmed it this week

badgeUnchecked.message: Flagship couldn't check this site's certificate yet

blockedLead.message: $1 served a certificate that your server $2 didn't sign.
blockedLead.description: Warning page: {0} site name, {1} server name

blockedExplain.message: Someone may be intercepting your connection to your server, for example with a certificate issued for its name without its knowledge. Nothing from this page was loaded.

blockedExpected.description: Warning page label above a fingerprint

blockedServed.description: Warning page label above a fingerprint

blockedUnknownFingerprint.description: Warning page: shown instead of a fingerprint

blockedAdvice.message: Don't sign in or enter anything on this site from this network. Try again from another network, or open the server in the Flagship app on your phone, which checks the same certificate.

blockedRecheck.description: Warning page button: asks the server for its signed certificate again

blockedStillWrong.message: Still not the certificate your server signed.

knockForeignTitle.description: Bar on a page showing a sign-in code for another site

knockForeignBody.message: This page shows a sign-in code for $1, not for this site ($2). Scanning it could sign someone else's browser in as you.
knockForeignBody.description: {0} the site the code is for, {1} this site

knockVerifiedTitle.description: Bar on a genuine sign-in page

knockVerifiedBody.message: It belongs to $1, and its certificate is the one your server signed. Sign in with the Flagship app.

knockUncheckedTitle.description: Bar on a sign-in page the extension can't fully check

knockNotYourServerBody.message: This site isn't on one of your paired servers, so the extension can't vouch for its certificate. Firefox's usual checks apply.

knockNotPairedBody.message: Pair the extension with the Flagship app to have it check your servers' certificates.

knockStaleBody.message: This site is on your server $1, but the extension couldn't confirm its certificate just now.

knockDirectUnboundBody.message: This sign-in is for your server $1, but the extension can't tell which server serves this address.

knockSignInButton.description: Sign-in bar button: opens the page's own app link

pairIntro.message: On your phone, open the Flagship app, scan this code, check that both screens show the same six digits, then pick a server and approve.

pairWaiting.message: Scan this code with the Flagship app.

pairMatching.message: Check that your phone shows the same code, then approve on the phone.

pairCodeHint.message: If the codes differ, cancel on the phone.

pairDone.message: Paired with $1. The extension now checks this server's certificate.

pairUnreachable.message: Couldn't reach Flagship. Check your connection and try again.

pairRelayClosed.message: The connection to the phone closed. Try again.

pairWrongKind.message: The phone sent a different kind of approval. Update the Flagship app and try again.

pairUnreadable.message: The phone sent something the extension can't read.

pairBadServer.message: The phone named a server the extension won't connect to.

pairRedeemFailed.message: The server didn't accept the pairing. Try again from the phone.

pairQrLabel.message: Pairing code for the Flagship app

pairNeverKeys.message: The extension never holds a key that can act as you. It can read only your server's signed certificate fingerprint, for 30 days, and you can end that from your phone at any time.

pairNeedsPermission.message: First allow the extension on Flagship sites, so it can reach your server and check its certificate.
pairNeedsPermission.description: Pairing page: shown until Firefox grants the site permission

pairGrantPermission.description: Pairing page button: asks Firefox for the site permission

popupSiteReload.message: Reload the page to check it.

popupSiteMatch.message: Certificate checked: it's the one $1 signed.

popupSiteMismatch.message: Stopped: this certificate isn't the one $1 signed.

popupSiteStale.message: Certificate matches, but $1 hasn't confirmed it this week.

popupSiteUnchecked.message: Couldn't check this certificate with $1 yet.

popupSiteUnknown.message: Not on one of your paired servers. Firefox's usual checks apply.

popupRevokeHint.message: To end a pairing, revoke “Firefox extension” under the server’s Remote or Browser sessions in the Flagship app.

popupSessionEnded.message: The server ended this pairing. Pair again to keep its certificate current.

popupSessionExpired.message: Pairing expired. Pair again to keep its certificate current.

popupForgetConfirm.message: Forget $1? The extension stops checking its certificate.

popupNeedsPermission.message: Allow the extension on Flagship sites so it can check their certificates.
